<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914033_theRebbe_108" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914033_theRebbe_108__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the connection between the two services of "turn from evil" and "do good" to the two Divine names Elokim and Havayah, where "turn from evil" involves fear of the King's command and relates to Elokim, while "do good" involves toiling in Torah and mitzvos beyond one's nature and relates to Havayah, the transcendent light.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is the connection of the two services of "turn from evil" and "do good" to the two names Elokim and Havayah.</t>
    <t s="1">For it is known</t>
    <t s="2">that in "turn from evil" is also included the caution not to transgress positive commandments</t>
    <t s="3">(for the nullification of a positive commandment is a prohibition,</t>
    <t s="4">evil),</t>
    <t s="5">except that in "turn from evil,"</t>
    <t s="6">since his caution in fulfilling the commandments is because he fears</t>
    <t s="7">to transgress the command of the King,</t>
    <t s="8">his fulfillment of the commandments is only to the extent that he is obligated.</t>
    <t s="9">And the innovation in the service of "do good" is,</t>
    <t s="10">that his fulfillment of the commandments is</t>
    <t s="11">(not only because he is compelled in this,</t>
    <t s="12">in order not to transgress the command,</t>
    <t s="13">but rather)</t>
    <t s="14">in a manner of "doing,"</t>
    <t s="15">and "do good."</t>
    <t s="16">And as it is explained in Likkutei Torah</t>
    <t s="17">that the concept of "and do good" is that he toils himself in Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="18">and even to the point of exertion beyond his nature and habit.</t>
    <t s="19">And this is that the service of "turn from evil" pertains to the name Elokim and the service of "do good" to the name Havayah,</t>
    <t s="20">because that he fears to transgress the commandments of the King,</t>
    <t s="21">and even to the point that from his fear he conquers his evil inclination</t>
    <t s="22">(even when his inclination burns like fire)</t>
    <t s="23">because he fears to transgress the command of the King,</t>
    <t s="24">is through his feeling that He, blessed be He, rules and dominates over him,</t>
    <t s="25">Elokim.</t>
    <t s="26">And the service of "do good,"</t>
    <t s="27">that he toils himself in Torah and mitzvos more than his nature and habit,</t>
    <t s="28">is through the revelation of the light of the Surrounding that is above worlds,</t>
    <t s="29">Havayah that is above nature.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section elaborates on the connection of "do good" to the Surrounding light, explaining that just as the Surrounding light relates to worlds only as fulfilling the will, so too the service of "do good" stems from love of Havayah that becomes his entire being, and it highlights the superiority of the service of "seek peace" (Torah study) over "do good," because Torah is the garment of the Primordial One, Atzmus Ein Sof, and in Torah study one becomes the King Himself.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And an explanation of the connection of the service of "do good" to the Surrounding light in more particularity,</t>
    <t s="2">it was explained above,</t>
    <t s="3">that even the Surrounding light has a connection to worlds,</t>
    <t s="4">except that the significance of the worlds with respect to the Surrounding light is</t>
    <t s="5">(not their existence,</t>
    <t s="6">but rather)</t>
    <t s="7">that through them the will is completed.</t>
    <t s="8">And likewise is it in the service of "do good,"</t>
    <t s="9">for since the service of "do good" is because he loves Havayah and desires to cleave to Him,</t>
    <t s="10">behold his service of G-d is connected with the existence of the person,</t>
    <t s="11">his love and his will.</t>
    <t s="12">Except that his love for Havayah is in a manner that this</t>
    <t s="13">(love of G-d)</t>
    <t s="14">becomes his entire being,</t>
    <t s="15">therefore his service of G-d is in a manner that he does not take into account the limitation of his nature.</t>
    <t s="16">And this is the superiority in the service of "seek peace,"</t>
    <t s="17">which is the occupation of Torah,</t>
    <t s="18">over the service of "do good,"</t>
    <t s="19">for the Torah is called "the parable of the Primordial One,"</t>
    <t s="20">that it is a parable and garment for the aspect of the Primordial One of the world,</t>
    <t s="21">namely for the Atzmus of Ein Sof that is not in the category of worlds at all,</t>
    <t s="22">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="23">the self-nullification of the occupation of Torah is utter self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="24">And as is explained in Torah Or</t>
    <t s="25">the difference between Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="26">that in the fulfillment of mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="27">the person who fulfills the mitzvos is like a servant who fulfills the command of the King,</t>
    <t s="28">for the existence of the servant is not the existence of the Master.</t>
    <t s="29">And even when his fulfillment of mitzvos is from love with delights,</t>
    <t s="30">nevertheless there is one who loves.</t>
    <t s="31">But not so in the study of Torah, he is the King Himself.</t>
    <t s="32">For when the occupation of Torah is with self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="33">then "and I place My words in your mouth,"</t>
    <t s="34">My actual words.</t>
    <t s="35">Meaning</t>
    <t s="36">(that it is not the person who speaks,</t>
    <t s="37">but rather)</t>
    <t s="38">that "the word of Havayah, this is the halachah"</t>
    <t s="39">speaks from within his throat.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section describes three levels of love of G-d corresponding to the three phrases "with all your heart," "with all your soul," and "with all your might," where the love of "with all your soul" comes from contemplating the Surrounding light leading to self-sacrifice, and the love of "with all your might" comes from the revelation of Atzmus Ein Sof, which is a self-nullification not from one's own will but from the aspect of G-dliness itself, paralleling the superiority of "seek peace" over "do good."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And now, likewise is it in the service of love of G-d,</t>
    <t s="2">that there are three levels in it.</t>
    <t s="3">"With all your heart,"</t>
    <t s="4">"with all your soul,"</t>
    <t s="5">"and with all your might."</t>
    <t s="6">And it is explained in many places,</t>
    <t s="7">that the love of "with all your heart" is through contemplation upon the G-dly light that is invested in creations to give them life,</t>
    <t s="8">which in general is the light that fills.</t>
    <t s="9">For by contemplating that the life-force of every thing is G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="10">and his contemplation is in a manner that this will be understood also in the intellect of the animal soul,</t>
    <t s="11">through this he will come to love Havayah "with all your heart, with both your inclinations."</t>
    <t s="12">And the love of "with all your soul" is through contemplation that the light that gives life to the worlds is merely an illumination and that this illumination is incomparable relative to Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="13">which in general is the Surrounding light,</t>
    <t s="14">through this he will come to the love of "with all your soul,"</t>
    <t s="15">that his love for Havayah is in a manner of self-sacrifice,</t>
    <t s="16">"even if He takes your soul."</t>
    <t s="17">And the love of "with all your might" is through the revelation of the Atzmus of Ein Sof that is not in the category of worlds at all,</t>
    <t s="18">that through this revelation,</t>
    <t s="19">the love is beyond measure and limitation.</t>
    <t s="20">And although even the love of "with all your soul" is "even if He takes your soul" and the matter of self-sacrifice is beyond measure and limitation,</t>
    <t s="21">nevertheless the self-sacrifice</t>
    <t s="22">that is in the love of "with all your soul,"</t>
    <t s="23">which is generally in the aspect of Chayah,</t>
    <t s="24">is in a manner that he wants to sacrifice his soul</t>
    <t s="25">[and moreover, this will is analogous to</t>
    <t s="26">the will based on reason,</t>
    <t s="27">from the aspect that all matters are incomparable relative to Ein Sof].</t>
    <t s="28">And the love of "with all your might,"</t>
    <t s="29">which is generally in the aspect of Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="30">is not from his will but because he cannot be separated, G-d forbid, from His Oneness.</t>
    <t s="31">For self-sacrifice in this manner is the true matter of self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="32">since the self-sacrifice is not from his will</t>
    <t s="33">(existence)</t>
    <t s="34">but from the aspect of G-dliness.</t>
    <t s="35">And analogous to what was explained above</t>
    <t s="36">(section 3)</t>
    <t s="37">regarding the superiority of the service of "seek peace" over the service of "do good."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
